\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{भविष्य} (bhaviṣya)}{भविष्य (bhaviṣya)}]{\mr{भविष्य} (bhaviṣya) — the future}

\label{lesson:MR-C160-bhavishya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for the past, then the Marathi for to happen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{भविष्य}}
\textbf{\mr{भविष्य}} — \emph{bhaviṣya} — \textquotedblleft{}the future\textquotedblright{}. Marathi's future adds endings to the verb: \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{जाईन}} — \emph{mī jāīn} — \textquotedblleft{}I will go\textquotedblright{}; \textbf{\mr{तो} \mr{जाईल}} — \emph{to jāīl} — \textquotedblleft{}he will go\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{भविष्य}} (\emph{bhaviṣya}) is Sanskrit \emph{bhaviṣya}, \textquotedblleft{}about to be, future\textquotedblright{}, taken over whole as a learned loan, a tatsama. It is built on \emph{bhū}, \textquotedblleft{}to be, become\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bhaviṣya}, once more

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{लवकरच} (lavkarac)}{लवकरच (lavkarac)}]{\mr{लवकरच} (lavkarac) — soon}

\label{lesson:MR-C160-lavkarac}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for to happen, then the Marathi for the future.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{लवकरच}}
\textbf{\mr{लवकरच}} — \emph{lavkarac} — \textquotedblleft{}soon\textquotedblright{}. \textbf{\mr{लवकर}}, \textquotedblleft{}early, quickly\textquotedblright{}, with the emphatic \textbf{\mr{च}}: \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{लवकरच} \mr{येईन}.} — \emph{mī lavkarac yeīn} — \textquotedblleft{}I will come soon.\textquotedblright{}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{लवकरच}} (\emph{lavkarac}) is \textbf{\mr{लवकर}}, \textquotedblleft{}early, soon\textquotedblright{}, with the emphatic \textbf{-\mr{च}}. The origin of \textbf{\mr{लवकर}} is not settled: neither CDIAL nor DEDR has an entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{पुढचा} / \mr{पुढची} / \mr{पुढचे} (puḍhcā / puḍhcī …)}{पुढचा / पुढची / पुढचे (puḍhcā / puḍhcī …)}]{\mr{पुढचा} / \mr{पुढची} / \mr{पुढचे} (puḍhcā / puḍhcī / puḍhce) — next}

\label{lesson:MR-C160-pudhca}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for the future, then the Marathi for soon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{पुढचा} / \mr{पुढची} / \mr{पुढचे}}
\textbf{\mr{पुढचा} / \mr{पुढची} / \mr{पुढचे}} — \emph{puḍhcā / puḍhcī / puḍhce} — \textquotedblleft{}next\textquotedblright{}. It agrees with its noun: \textbf{\mr{पुढच्या} \mr{आठवड्यात}} — \emph{puḍhcyā āṭhavḍyāt} — \textquotedblleft{}next week\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{पुढचा}} (\emph{puḍhcā}) is \textbf{\mr{पुढे}}, \textquotedblleft{}ahead\textquotedblright{}, with the possessive ending \emph{-cā}, \textquotedblleft{}of\textquotedblright{}. The origin of \textbf{\mr{पुढे}} is not settled: neither CDIAL nor DEDR has an entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{यानंतर} (yānantar)}{यानंतर (yānantar)}]{\mr{यानंतर} (yānantar) — from now on, after this}

\label{lesson:MR-C160-yanantar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for soon, then the Marathi for next.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{यानंतर}}
\textbf{\mr{यानंतर}} — \emph{yānantar} — \textquotedblleft{}from now on, after this\textquotedblright{}. It is \textbf{\mr{या}}, \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\mr{नंतर}}, \textquotedblleft{}after\textquotedblright{}: \textbf{\mr{यानंतर} \mr{मी} \mr{रोज} \mr{चालेन}.} — \emph{yānantar mī roj cālen} — \textquotedblleft{}From now on I will walk every day.\textquotedblright{}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{यानंतर}} (\emph{yānantar}) is \emph{yā-}, \textquotedblleft{}this\textquotedblright{}, with \textbf{\mr{नंतर}}, \textquotedblleft{}after\textquotedblright{}, which comes from Sanskrit \emph{anantaram}, \textquotedblleft{}immediately after\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 287).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{आखणे} (ākhṇe)}{आखणे (ākhṇe)}]{\mr{आखणे} (ākhṇe) — to plan, to draw up}

\label{lesson:MR-C160-akhne}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for next, then the Marathi for from now on.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{आखणे}}
\textbf{\mr{आखणे}} — \emph{ākhṇe} — \textquotedblleft{}to plan, to draw up\textquotedblright{}. Said of a plan or a line: \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{प्रवासाची} \mr{योजना} \mr{आखीन}.} — \emph{mī pravāsācī yojanā ākhīn} — \textquotedblleft{}I will plan the trip.\textquotedblright{}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{आखणे}} (\emph{ākhṇe}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{aṅkayati}, \textquotedblleft{}marks, brands\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 104). CDIAL glosses the Marathi verb \textquotedblleft{}to mark, trace\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{मी} \mr{जाईन} (mī jāīn)}{मी जाईन (mī jāīn)}]{\mr{मी} \mr{जाईन} (mī jāīn) — the future, person by person}

\label{lesson:MR-C160-jain}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}to plan\textquotedblright{}, then \textquotedblleft{}tomorrow\textquotedblright{}, then \textbf{\mr{उद्या} \mr{भेटू}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: who will do it?}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{उद्या} \mr{मी} \mr{पुण्याला} \mr{जाईन}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{udyā mī puṇyālā jāīn.} — \textquotedblleft{}Tomorrow I will go to Pune.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Use \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{जाईन}}, \textbf{\mr{तू} \mr{जाशील}}, \textbf{\mr{तो} / \mr{ती} \mr{जाईल}}, \textbf{\mr{आम्ही} \mr{जाऊ}}, \textbf{\mr{तुम्ही} \mr{जाल}}, \textbf{\mr{ते} \mr{जातील}}. The future changes with the person, but not gender: a man and a woman both say \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{जाईन}}.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a few future stems}
The endings stay while the stem changes: \textbf{\mr{येणे} $\to$ \mr{येईन} / \mr{येईल}}, \textbf{\mr{करणे} $\to$ \mr{करीन} / \mr{करेल}}, \textbf{\mr{वाचणे} $\to$ \mr{वाचीन} / \mr{वाचेल}}, \textbf{\mr{पडणे} $\to$ \mr{पडेल}}. Ask \textbf{\mr{काय} \mr{होईल}?}, \textquotedblleft{}What will happen?\textquotedblright{}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}Tomorrow I will go to Pune\textquotedblright{} — \emph{udyā mī puṇyālā jāīn}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}It will rain in the evening\textquotedblright{} — \emph{sandhyākāḷī pāūs paḍel}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}We will meet tomorrow\textquotedblright{} — \emph{āmhī udyā bheṭū}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}I will go\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{जाईन}}.) \textquotedblleft{}We will go\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{जाऊ}}.) \textquotedblleft{}You will go\textquotedblright{} with respect? (\textbf{\mr{जाल}}.) \textquotedblleft{}They will go\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{जातील}}.) \textquotedblleft{}It will rain\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{पडेल}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{मी} \mr{जाणार} \mr{आहे} (mī jāṇār āhe)}{मी जाणार आहे (mī jāṇār āhe)}]{\mr{मी} \mr{जाणार} \mr{आहे} (mī jāṇār āhe) — a plan, and what will not happen}

\label{lesson:MR-C160-janar-ahe}



\begin{quote}
Say \textquotedblleft{}I will go\textquotedblright{}, then \textbf{\mr{जाणे}}, then \textbf{\mr{आहे}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: -\mr{णार} \mr{आहे} for a plan}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mr{पुढच्या} \mr{आठवड्यात} \mr{मी} \mr{गावाला} \mr{जाणार} \mr{आहे}.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{puḍhcyā āṭhavḍyāt mī gāvālā jāṇār āhe.} — \textquotedblleft{}Next week I am going to go to the village.\textquotedblright{}
\end{quote}

Take \textbf{-\mr{णे}} off the verb and add \textbf{-\mr{णार}}: \textbf{\mr{जाणे} $\to$ \mr{जाणार}}, \textbf{\mr{करणे} $\to$ \mr{करणार}}, \textbf{\mr{येणे} $\to$ \mr{येणार}}. Add \textbf{\mr{आहे}} for a present plan. \textbf{-\mr{णार}} stays the same with every person in this bounded A2 pattern.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: -\mr{णार} \mr{नाही} for won't}
Replace \textbf{\mr{आहे}} with \textbf{\mr{नाही}} for a future refusal or firm negative: \textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{उद्या} \mr{येणार} \mr{नाही}}, \textquotedblleft{}I won't come tomorrow.\textquotedblright{}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I am going to go to the village\textquotedblright{} — \emph{mī gāvālā jāṇār āhe}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I am going to work tomorrow\textquotedblright{} — \emph{mī udyā kām karṇār āhe}
  \item \textquotedblleft{}I won't come tomorrow\textquotedblright{} — \emph{mī udyā yeṇār nāhī}
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
\textquotedblleft{}I will go\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{जाईन}}.) \textquotedblleft{}I am going to go\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{जाणार} \mr{आहे}}.) \textquotedblleft{}I won't come\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{मी} \mr{येणार} \mr{नाही}}.) \textquotedblleft{}Next week\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{पुढच्या} \mr{आठवड्यात}}.) \textquotedblleft{}From now on\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{यानंतर}}.) \textquotedblleft{}To plan\textquotedblright{}? (\textbf{\mr{आखणे}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
